what_worked: Four-signal filter framework is genuinely original; bridge sentences between every insight create exceptional narrative flow.
fix_next: Recompute all median values against the actual dataset; the B2B 5.7x headline claim appears substantially overstated versus reference 2.35x.
verdict: Superb narrative architecture undermined by multiple inaccurate median values and an inflated headline claim.
factual_error_detail: Slide 10: B2B median $1,036/B2C $181 yields 5.7x but reference median multiple is 2.35x — headline claim overstated. Slide 8: AI median $446 vs reference $503; Marketing $1,586 vs $2,370; Dev Tools $185 vs $635 — all materially off. Slide 6: mean $13,472 implies total ~$13.47M vs reference $15.60M. Slide 13: Stripe n=644 vs reference 636. Slide 7: 20% zero-revenue (200 listings) vs reference 216 (21.6%) — minor but denominator unclear. Slide 2/6: top-10% share 82% not directly verifiable but top-10 share is 49.6% per reference, so 82% for top-100 is plausible but unverified.

evidence.insight: The four-signal filter (B2B, DR, payment stack, followers-as-noise) is a genuinely useful synthesis beyond chart description. Insight 10 closing the loop back to Insight 1 (concentration is reinforcing) shows real analytical thinking. The vanity-metric debunking adds decision value.
evidence.narrative: Every insight slide ends with an explicit arrow-bridge sentence connecting to the next. The three-chapter funnel metaphor on slide 3 creates a single coherent argument. Synthesis slide 18 and bottom-line slide 19 land the conclusion cleanly. One of the strongest narrative arcs seen.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets context (dataset, date, author). Appendix slide 20 acknowledges self-reported data and missing fields. However, missingness rates for key fields (category 27.4%, audience_type 28.8%) are never quantified, which matters critically for the B2B and category analyses. Target audience is implied but never explicitly stated.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple median values diverge materially from reference: AI $446 vs $503, Marketing $1,586 vs $2,370, Dev Tools $185 vs $635. The deck's headline B2B premium of 5.7x appears substantially overstated vs reference 2.35x median multiple. Mean $13,472 implies ~$13.47M total vs $15.60M reference. Stripe count 644 vs 636. These are not rounding differences — several are 50%+ off.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette, clean bar charts, effective callout boxes with key stats. Progress dots track position through 10 insights. Section dividers are clean. Donut chart on slide 7 is a weak choice; correlation chart on slide 12 comparing only two bars is visually thin. Template is polished but every insight slide follows identical layout, becoming repetitive.
evidence.ai_slop: STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL footer on every slide is performative consulting theater. Template is highly uniform — identical layout (chart left, callout right, bridge bottom) across all insight slides. Polished but formulaic; not egregious filler.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 5.5 to 4.5: the B2B 5.7x headline claim is the deck's central finding and appears roughly 2.4x overstated versus reference (2.35x); Marketing and Dev Tools medians are off by 33-70%; mean revenue implies a total ~$2.1M below reference. Reduced bonus from 2 to 1: the narrative craft is strong but the factual foundation is too unreliable for full bonus credit.
